Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixcloud.com>; Legal <legal@helixcloud.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 20:05:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — jurisdiction and emergency relief

Marcus — thanks for the draft. A couple of high-level asks from legal here:

1) We operate in NA + APAC; our security team is sensitive to US-only governing law. Can Redwood accept a split choice of law (California for commercial terms; Singapore for data-security carve) or do you prefer a single seat?
2) We need an explicit carve for emergency injunctive relief that allows us to seek preservation orders in local courts (APAC). Can you confirm Redwood’s stance on non-waivable provisional measures?

I attached the redlines (v3) with comments. Procurement would like to keep this moving — our preferred timeline is to finish legal review this week and turn to procurement signatures next week.

-Michael
HelixCloud — Senior Counsel

Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — jurisdiction and emergency relief

Thanks Michael — looping in our legal lead (Kimberly) and sales lead (Lauren) to coordinate trade-offs. Quick points from our side: 

- Redwood prefers a single governing law for clarity and SLO enforcement; California is our standard. However, we are open to a limited split for narrowly-drawn data-security carve if HelixCloud can commit to an escalation lane that routes security disputes to Redwood’s Singapore data-security liaison.

- On emergency injunctive relief: we accept carving out provisional measures for preservation, but want to preserve our right to seek expedited relief in California courts when availability of equitable relief is necessary to protect Redwood’s infrastructure or IP.

Action items I see: Kimberly to propose compromise redline language that: (a) permits local preservation measures, (b) keeps seat at CA for final relief, and (c) defines an explicit ‘break-glass’ notification and coordination process so both sides can seek immediate local orders without triggering litigation game-playing.

I’ve attached the order form PDF as reference. Lauren — can you confirm HelixCloud’s procurement deadline?

Thanks,
Marcus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — jurisdiction and emergency relief

Michael / Marcus / team —

I reviewed HelixCloud’s comments and drafted compromise language. Notes below and inserted comments in the redline doc: 1) Governing law: single law (California) for interpretation of the MSA and Order Form, with a narrowly scoped data-security clause that references applicable local law for notification and breach remediation obligations only. This keeps enforcement predictable while acknowledging local incident response requirements.

2) Emergency / provisional measures: proposed two-tier approach:
   - Tier A (Preservation): Either party may seek immediate local provisional relief (seizure/preservation/temporary restraining orders) in the jurisdiction where evidence or impacted systems reside. Such measures are limited in scope and duration and must be immediately escalated via the break-glass process.
   - Tier B (Final injunctive relief): For remedies that exceed preservation (ongoing injunctive relief affecting core service operations or IP), parties agree to submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of California courts unless an arbitration seat is agreed in writing.

3) Arbitration fallback: We can accept arbitration as the default for most commercial disputes (Monetary claims, performance) with Clarified emergency carveouts for court-based provisional relief as above.

Break-glass process (proposed):
- Immediate teleconference with designated security/ops contacts within 2 hours of filing emergency relief;
- Simultaneous notice to Redwood legal (redwood-legal@redwood.com) and Helix legal;
- Documentation within 48 hours summarizing facts and any orders obtained;
- Agreement not to use preservation measures to secure a strategic advantage in the main dispute (sanctions clause if abused).

I’ll attach the updated redline with exact text. Rishi — please review the sanctions wording (penalty for misuse) and confirm whether our SLA/availability exceptions need explicit carve language.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 08:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — jurisdiction and emergency relief

Kimberly — thanks, this is the most productive framing yet. A few comments from HelixCloud: 

- We can accept California governing law for contract interpretation, provided we preserve the right to seek local provisional measures in APAC without pre-approval. The break-glass notification requirement is acceptable.
- Regarding the sanctions clause: HelixCloud will not agree to a one-way penalty. We propose a mutual ‘abuse’ standard with a three-step escalation (notice, cure opportunity where feasible, capped fee if misuse is demonstrated).
- On arbitration: we prefer arbitration in Singapore for commercial disputes (neutral seat + enforceability in APAC) rather than CA, but can live with CA if Redwood is firm. Alternatively, we suggest arbitration with a bifurcated emergency procedure that allows courts to hear provisional measures.

Procurement note: our target for sign is 2027-10-29. We need the final legal text by COB 2027-10-22 to make that timeline.

-Michael
